overview: ARM-FM leverages Foundation Models to automatically generate Language-Aligned Reward Machines (LARMs) from natural language task descriptions, and integrates them into RL training by conditioning policies on language embeddings of RM states to provide dense structured rewards, enable compositional skill reuse, and achieve zero-shot generalization across diverse sparse-reward environments.

modules.name: LARM Formal Data Structure
modules.description: Defines the core Language-Aligned Reward Machine formalism, extending the standard RM tuple (U, u_I, Σ, δ, R, F, L) with natural language instructions l_u per RM state and an embedding function φ(·) mapping instructions to embedding vectors z_u. Includes data classes for RM states, transitions, reward specifications, and the complete LARM object with serialization/deserialization support.

modules.name: FM-Driven LARM Generation (Generator)
modules.description: Implements the iterative generator FM component that takes a high-level natural language prompt and visual observation to produce a complete LARM specification. Handles prompt construction for RM structure generation (states, transitions, rewards), ensuring adherence to the required plaintext format. Supports the self-improvement loop by incorporating critic feedback from previous rounds.

modules.name: FM-Driven LARM Critic and Refinement Loop
modules.description: Implements the critic FM component and the N-round self-improvement loop. The critic evaluates generated LARMs on correctness, compactness, completeness, mission logic, and format adherence. Includes human-in-the-loop integration where a human operator can replace or supplement the critic at any round. Manages iterative refinement until convergence or human approval.

modules.name: Labeling Function Code Generation
modules.description: Generates executable Python boolean-predicate functions for each RM event symbol using the FM. Each function inspects environment attributes to determine if a symbolic event has occurred. Includes the separate generator and critic prompts for labeling function correctness, and ensures generated code is sandboxed, validated against the environment API, and aligned with the RM specification.

modules.name: Language Embedding Module
modules.description: Implements the embedding function φ(·) that maps natural language RM state instructions to dense embedding vectors using a foundation model's text encoder. Supports batched embedding computation for all RM states, caching of embeddings to avoid recomputation, and provides the interface for conditioning RL policies on the current RM state's embedding z_u.

modules.name: Augmented MDP Environment Wrapper
modules.description: Constructs the cross-product MDP M' = S × U from the original MDP and the LARM. Wraps standard RL environments to maintain the current RM state, execute the labeling function on each transition to detect events, update the RM state via the transition function δ, and compute the combined reward R_total = R_MDP + R_RM. Provides the augmented observation (s_t, z_{u_t}) to the agent.

modules.name: DQN + LARM Training Agent
modules.description: Adapts the Deep Q-Network algorithm for LARM-augmented environments. The Q-network takes as input the concatenation of environment state and language embedding of the current RM state. Implements augmented experience replay storing transitions (s, u, a, R_total, s', u'), and the modified target computation. Used for MiniGrid and BabyAI experiments.

modules.name: PPO + LARM Training Agent
modules.description: Adapts the Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm for LARM-augmented environments. The policy and value networks are conditioned on language embeddings of the current RM state. Implements vectorized rollouts compatible with the augmented MDP wrapper. Used for the Craftium 3D Minecraft-based experiments with higher computational demands.

modules.name: SAC + LARM Training Agent
modules.description: Adapts the Soft Actor-Critic algorithm for LARM-augmented environments with continuous action spaces. The actor and critic networks receive the language embedding of the current RM state as additional input. Supports optional combination with intrinsic exploration rewards (e.g., RND). Used for Meta-World robotic manipulation experiments.

modules.name: Rainbow DQN + LARM Training Agent
modules.description: Adapts the Rainbow DQN algorithm (combining N-step learning, prioritized replay, distributional RL, etc.) for LARM-augmented environments. The Q-network is conditioned on language embeddings of RM states, enabling multi-task generalization. Used for the XLand-MiniGrid multi-task experiments.

modules.name: Multi-Task Training Pipeline
modules.description: Implements the multi-task training framework where a single policy is trained simultaneously on multiple environments, each with its own LARM. Manages the union of sub-goal embeddings across all tasks, ensuring the shared policy can leverage semantically similar subtasks. Handles environment sampling, episode management, and per-task reward tracking.

modules.name: Zero-Shot Generalization Evaluator
modules.description: Implements the zero-shot generalization evaluation protocol. Given a policy trained on tasks {A, B} with LARMs R_A, R_B, evaluates it on a novel composite task C with a newly generated LARM R_C. Checks whether sub-goal embeddings in R_C are semantically close to embeddings seen during training, enabling skill reuse without fine-tuning. Reports success rate on unseen tasks.

modules.name: LLM-as-Judge Quality Evaluator
modules.description: Implements the automated evaluation of FM-generated LARMs using a separate judge FM. Evaluates syntactic correctness of RM structures and labeling function code across a large set of generated tasks. Produces correctness scores for different FM scales, enabling the scaling trend analysis shown in the paper's ablation study.

modules.name: Embedding Space Visualization and Analysis
modules.description: Implements PCA-based visualization of language embeddings from thousands of RM state instructions across generated tasks. Clusters and color-codes embeddings by semantic category (start, middle, end states) to verify the semantic coherence of the embedding space. Validates that semantically similar sub-tasks from different tasks cluster together, confirming the foundation for skill transfer.

modules.name: Experiment Configuration and Logging Infrastructure
modules.description: Manages experiment configurations including hyperparameters for all RL agents (DQN, PPO, SAC, Rainbow), environment specifications, LARM generation parameters, and evaluation protocols. Integrates with TensorBoard/WandB for training curve logging, handles multiple random seed execution, result aggregation with mean and standard deviation, and automated generation of comparison plots and tables.
